verdict.rationale: Turso's core engine can run outside Turso Cloud. libSQL is an MIT-licensed open-source fork with a server mode, the local-development docs start a local libSQL server, and the embedded database runs entirely in-process. The site also claims bring-your-own-cloud deployment. However, the evidence only documents local and development use; managed features like branching, PITR, the Platform API and MCP are tied to Turso Cloud, and BYOC is a one-line marketing claim. missing for 10: documented production self-hosting guide for the server, evidence that cloud features (branching, PITR, platform API) can be self-hosted, detail on BYOC deployment, independent hands-on self-hosting reports.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: libSQL is an open source, open contribution fork of SQLite, created and maintained by Turso.
It adds new features on top of SQLite, such as vector search, replication, server mode, and more. libSQL is open source (MIT license).
This will start a local libSQL server and create a database for you.
run entirely in your process, no server needed
